optio_gaius.name: Optio Gaius
optio_gaius.examine: The cohort's optio. He has the look of a man who has counted a great many recruits.
idle: Keep your blade clean and your mouth shut, and the auxilia will make something of you.

gallic_merchant.name: Gaulish merchant
gallic_merchant.examine: A Gaulish merchant with rings on every finger.
idle: Fine linen, fair prices! Well, prices.
Keep your hands where I can see them, friend.

sacerdos.name: Sacerdos
sacerdos.examine: The temple priest of Castra Ferrea, smelling of incense and old wine.
idle: The gods notice what you give them, and what you don't.

harbourmaster.name: Harbourmaster Lucilla
harbourmaster.examine: She runs the harbour with a wax tablet in one hand and a boathook in the other.
idle: Tide's turning. If you're not buying or fishing, you're in the way.

fishmonger.name: Fishmonger
fishmonger.examine: A weathered fishwife with forearms like a smith's.
idle: Fresh from the boats! Well, fresh-ish.

centurion_varro.name: Centurion Varro
centurion_varro.examine: The centurion who holds the gate in the limes. His crest has seen better days.
idle: Nothing comes over that palisade without my say. Plenty goes over it without coming back.

procurator.name: Procurator metallorum
procurator.examine: The emperor's man at the mines. Every ingot passes under his stamp.
idle: Silver for the treasury, lead for the pipes, and a stamp on every bar. That's Vipasca.
If you're not buying, mining, or paying a fine, you're loitering.

foreman_masculus.name: Foreman Masculus
foreman_masculus.examine: The pit foreman. He moves slowly and stiffly, like a man made of plaster.
idle: Mind the gallery. Mind your eyes.
My knees haven't bent properly since the spring. Don't ask.

melissa.name: Melissa the shepherd
melissa.examine: A shepherd girl with a crook taller than she is, and no sheep.
idle: Baa. That's all I've got left: the noise.
Father says the hollow's no place for a girl. It's no place for sheep either, now.

baker_sabina.name: Sabina the baker
baker_sabina.examine: The fort's baker, floured to the elbows. She feeds six hundred men a day.
idle: Mind the stall. Bread doesn't grow on trees, you know. It grows in fields.

smith_tertius.name: Tertius the smith
smith_tertius.examine: The fort's smith: arms like hams, eyebrows singed off years ago.
idle: Hot iron waits for no one. Neither do I.

legate_sertorius.name: Legate Sertorius
legate_sertorius.examine: The legate of the legion, in Rome to report to the Senate. He looks at you the way he'd look at a horse he might buy.
idle: The Senate wants victories. I want centurions who come back from them.

tiro.name: Tiro
tiro.summary: Enlist in the auxilia at Castra Ferrea and prove you can fight with blade, sling, and curse.
start: Another peregrinus looking for a future? Good. The Emperor needs auxilia more than he needs another farmer.
Serve twenty-five years and you leave a citizen. Serve badly and you leave in a box.
First I want to see you fight. Here: a sling, some lead, a lituus, and a few binding tablets. Don't lose them.
Strike the training dummy with your blade. Then with the sling. Then curse it, if you have the stomach for it.

steps.log: Strike the training dummy six times with a melee weapon.
remind: The dummy is by the forum. Six good blows with a blade. Go on.

steps.log: Wield the sling and hit the training dummy five times.
remind: Wield the sling, wear the lead as ammunition, and put five into the dummy.

steps.log: Wield the lituus and curse the training dummy three times.
remind: Lituus in hand, tablets ready. Three curses on the dummy. The Manes won't mind; it's only straw.

steps.log: Kill three of the rats in the granary.
remind: The granary rats are eating the cohort's grain. Kill three and we'll call it your first campaign.

steps.log: Report back to Optio Gaius.

complete: Three rats. The poets will sing of it. Still, you did what you were told, and that's rarer than courage.
From today you're a tiro of the cohort. Take this parma; it's seen better arms than yours.
When you've the coin, the quartermaster's stores are open to you. Iron, not bronze. Look after it.

miles.name: Miles
miles.summary: Earn your place in the line: deal with the wolves on the woods road, mend the palisade, and scout the old barrow.
start: Back again, tiro? Good. Recruits who come back are recruits worth feeding.
Wolves have been taking the cohort's mules on the woods road. Thin the pack. Five should teach the rest some manners.
The north palisade is rotting, too. Bring me ten logs and fifteen bronze nails, and the carpenters will do the rest.
And there's talk of lights at the old barrow, north-west past the woods. Go and look. Only look.

steps.log: Kill five wolves in the frontier woods.
remind: Five wolves. They're north of the gate, past the sign. Bring food.

steps.log: Bring Optio Gaius 10 logs and 15 bronze nails for the palisade.
remind: Ten logs and fifteen bronze nails. Chop the trees west of the fort, and the smithy can make the nails.

steps.log: Scout the old barrow north-west of the woods.
remind: The barrow is north-west, past the woods. Just look at it and come back.

steps.log: Report what you saw at the barrow to Optio Gaius.

complete: Lemures, at the barrow door? Then the stories are true, and I'll need to write to the prefect.
You did well. From today you're a miles of the cohort: a soldier, not a recruit.
Take this mail. A lorica hamata has turned more blades than prayers have. The armoury is open to you now.

rewards.unlocks: Mail and heavier arms from the quartermaster (Optio Gaius)
rewards.title: Miles of the auxilia

duplicarius.name: Duplicarius
duplicarius.summary: Find out who has been stealing the cohort's pay, and bring it back.
start: Silver has been going missing from the strongroom, a little every week. Pay day is in nine days.
Someone in the forum is fencing it. The Gaulish merchant hears everything that's sold in this town; ask him.
You've light fingers yourself, I hear. Good. It takes a thief to catch one.

steps.log: Ask the Gaulish merchant in the forum about the stolen silver.
remind: The merchant has a stall-side spot in the forum. Ask him who's been selling cohort silver.

steps.log: Deal with the latro on the road south-west of the fort and recover the pay chest.
remind: The merchant says a latro on the south-west road has been paying in cohort silver. Find him.

steps.log: Bring the stolen pay chest back to Optio Gaius.
remind: Bring me the chest. Unopened, if you value your skin.

complete: Every coin, near enough. The men will be paid, and they won't know how close it came.
Double pay for a soldier who saves the pay. You're a duplicarius now, and you'll ride with the ala when it comes.
A rider needs a longer reach. Take this spatha. The quartermaster has more, for those who earn them.

decurio.name: Decurio
decurio.summary: Lay the Larva in the barrow to rest, earn your discharge, and become a citizen of Rome.
start: The lemures in the barrow are restless again, and the men know why. Something old has woken in the depths: a larva.
Swords won't touch it. The sacerdos knows the old rite of the Lemuria; go to him first.
Do this, and I'll put your name forward for the decurionate. And after that, your discharge, and the citizenship that comes with it.

steps.log: Ask the sacerdos about the rite of the Lemuria.
remind: The sacerdos keeps the temple by the forum. Ask him about the Lemuria.

steps.log: Keep the black beans with you, go down into the barrow's depths, and lay the Larva to rest.
remind: Nine black beans, carried with you. Without them your blade passes through the thing like smoke.

steps.log: Report to Optio Gaius.

complete: The larva is gone, and the lemures are quiet. The men can sleep, which is more than I've done for a week.
You came here a peregrinus. You leave the auxilia a decurio, honourably discharged, and a citizen of Rome.
Here: your diploma. Two bronze tablets, seven witnesses. Keep them safe; your sons will want to see them.

rewards.unlocks: Roman citizenship (the legions, the capital, and a villa will open to citizens in time)
rewards.title: Civis Romanus

harpies_at_the_harbour.name: Harpies at the Harbour
harpies_at_the_harbour.summary: Drive off the harpies that rob the Portus boats, and help the fishmonger mend the nets they tore.
start: You there, with the sword. Can you use it?
Harpies. They come down off the eastern rocks when the boats land, snatch the catch, and shred the nets. Last week they took a child's hat. Just the hat.
Kill four of them and bring me feathers to prove it. The guild pays bounty on proof, not on stories.

steps.log: Kill four harpies on the eastern rocks.
remind: The rocks east of the beach. Four of them, and mind your eyes.

steps.log: Bring Harbourmaster Lucilla three harpy feathers.
remind: Feathers. Three. The guild's clerk counts them.

steps.log: Bring the fishmonger two bolts of linen to mend the nets.
remind: The nets are in ribbons. The fishmonger needs linen thread to mend them: two bolts. The Gaulish merchant in Castra Ferrea sells it.

steps.log: Report to Harbourmaster Lucilla.

complete: Nets mended, harpies thinned, and the boats coming home full. The guild's grateful, which means I am.
Here's your bounty. And a trick the archers on the grain ships use: fletch with harpy feathers. They fly true in any wind.
Bring me more feathers and you'll never run short of good arrows.

the_lost_eagle.name: The Lost Eagle
the_lost_eagle.summary: Recover the eagle of a cohort lost beyond the Limes from the war-chief who took it.
start: You've the look of someone who's killed things. Good. Listen.
Twenty years ago a cohort marched north from this gate and never came back. The raiders took their eagle. Hrodgar wears it like a trophy at his fires.
No legion forgets its eagle. Scout their camp, thin their spears, and bring it home.

steps.log: Scout the raiders' camp north of the gate in the limes.
remind: Follow the path north from the gate. Their camp is where the smoke is.

steps.log: Kill four Germanic raiders.
remind: Thin them out before you go for the war-chief. Four should do it.

steps.log: Defeat Hrodgar the War-chief in his clearing and take back the eagle.
remind: Hrodgar holds the clearing north of the camp, ringed with stones. When he throws, don't be where he's aiming.

steps.log: Bring the eagle to Centurion Varro at the gate.
remind: You have it? Then bring it here. Gods, bring it here.

complete: That's her. Tarnished, but that's her.
The whole frontier will hear of this by nightfall. Take this, and something more: the raiders' goldsmiths taught a captive of ours to twist a torc. I'll teach you.

the_silent_gallery.name: The Silent Gallery
the_silent_gallery.summary: Miners who work Vipasca's deep gallery come up stiff as statues. Clear it, and help the procurator make his silver quota.
start: You. You look like you can swing more than a pickaxe.
The deep gallery has gone quiet. The men I send down come back up slow and grey, if they come back at all, and the treasury doesn't accept excuses in place of silver.
Talk to Foreman Masculus at the pit. He went down last. He can tell you what's in there, if he can still move his jaw.

steps.log: Talk to Foreman Masculus by the pit.
remind: The foreman's by the pit, on the track south of town. You'll know him. He moves like a statue.
say: Basilisks. A whole nest of them at the gallery mouth, came up out of the old workings in the spring.
One looked at me. Just looked. My arms went heavy as lead, and I've walked like this ever since.
Don't meet their eyes. My grandfather fought in the east; he said they used polished bronze, so the beast saw only itself. Three bronze bars and a silver one, polished bright, at an anvil.

steps.log: Kill four basilisks at the mouth of the deep gallery.
remind: A mirror shield, friend. Three bronze bars and a silver one at an anvil. Then four of them, and the men can go back down.

steps.log: Bring the procurator five silver bars to make up the quota.
remind: The gallery's clear? Good. Now the quota. Five bars of silver, smelted and stamped. The furnace is behind you.

steps.log: Report to the procurator.

complete: Five bars, and the gallery working again. The treasury will be very nearly pleased.
Here's your fee, and something better: I'll sell you the good steel picks we keep for the gallery crews, and coal from the stores.
Masculus says his knees are coming back. He wants you to know. I wanted you to know that I don't care, but well done.

rewards.unlocks: The procurator sells steel pickaxes and coal

the_shepherds_flock.name: The Shepherd's Flock
the_shepherds_flock.summary: The cyclopes have taken a shepherd's flock up to their hollow in the hills of Seriphos. Drive them off.
start: You've got a sword. Good. I've got a crook, and that's not enough.
The cyclopes came down out of the hills at the new moon and took Father's whole flock. Forty ewes, up to that hollow past the temple, behind the rocks.
Father won't go. The last man who went came back without his boots, and without his feet in them. Please. Drive them off, and I'll make it worth your while.

steps.log: Drive off the cyclopes: kill four in the hollow in the hills.
remind: Up the path past the temple of Athena, into the hills. Four of them, and they throw rocks. Big ones.

steps.log: Bring Melissa three cyclops cheeses: they made it from her father's ewes.
remind: They'll have been milking our ewes, the thieves. Bring me some of their cheese, three wheels: it's ours by rights.
say: That's Father's cheese. I'd know it anywhere: the ewes graze on thyme, and you can taste it.
Three wheels. I'll take them down to him. He'll cry. He's always crying. Now he'll be crying about something good.

steps.log: Tell Melissa the hollow is clear.

complete: The flock's coming down! I can hear the bells from here.
Here: it's not much, but it's what we have. And I'll tell Nikias to keep your cheese for you. The cyclopes won't be making any more, so we will.
If you're ever hungry on Seriphos, you know where the good cheese is.

sacramentum.name: Sacramentum
sacramentum.summary: Swear the legionary's oath and join the legion: sacrifice to the gods, prove yourself on the limes, and turn out in a legionary's kit.
start: A citizen, are you? Then the auxilia's done with you, and the legion might not be.
A legionary swears the sacramentum before the gods. Take wine and incense to the sacerdos in the fort, so it's done properly.
Then show me you can hold the limes, and come back dressed like a legionary, not a farmer with a sword.

steps.log: Bring the sacerdos in Castra Ferrea a jug of wine and five measures of incense for the oath's sacrifice.
remind: Wine for the libation and incense for the altar. The gods won't hear an oath sworn on an empty hand.

steps.log: Prove yourself on the limes: kill eight Germanic raiders beyond the palisade.
remind: Eight raiders. The gate's behind me, and they're out there.

steps.log: Report to Centurion Varro with a legionary's kit: a steel scutum and ten steel pila.
remind: A scutum and ten pila. Steel. The smith knows the pattern, if you don't.

complete: Raise your hand. Repeat after me: to follow the emperor wherever he leads, never to desert the standards, never to shirk death for Rome.
Good. You're a legionary now, for twenty-five years or until we bury you.
Keep the scutum. And put this on: a lorica segmentata. The quartermaster will sell you another when you break that one.

rewards.unlocks: The lorica segmentata from the quartermaster
rewards.title: Miles legionis

optio.name: Optio
optio.summary: Patrols on Seriphos are coming back as statues. Find out why from the shepherdess, deal with the gorgons, and bring proof to Centurion Varro.
start: The governor sent a patrol to Seriphos. They came back. As statues, by the ferry, standing to attention.
There's a shepherdess on that island who sees everything that walks the hills. Start with her.
Bring me proof it's done, and I'll need an optio I can trust.

steps.log: Ask Melissa on Seriphos what happened to the patrol.
remind: The shepherdess on Seriphos. Go and ask her.

steps.log: Melissa says the patrol went into the ruins in the south-west. Kill three of the gorgons nesting there, and don't look them in the eye.
remind: The ruins, in the south-west of the island. A mirror shield, if you've any sense.

steps.log: Bring the gorgon's head back to Centurion Varro on the limes. Keep the sack closed.
remind: Don't open that here.

complete: Is that... no, don't show me. I believe you.
You've done the governor a service, and he remembers names. So do I. You're my optio now: my second, my stick, and my eyes.
Wear these. Phalerae, for valour. The men will see them before they see you.

bread_for_the_garrison.name: Bread for the Garrison
bread_for_the_garrison.summary: The fort's baker is short of flour with a cohort to feed. Grind some at the quern by the fields, then bake her a few loaves.
start: Six hundred soldiers, and the mill cart's stuck in the mud on the Vipasca road. They'll eat their own boots by Saturnalia.
There's a quern out by the fields, past the south gate. Grind me five pots of flour, would you? The Gaulish merchant sells seed wheat if you'd rather grow your own.
And then I'll show you what to do with it.

steps.log: Grind five pots of flour at the quern by the fields south of the fort (wheat from the grain fields, or from the Gaulish merchant's seed), and bring them to Sabina.
remind: Five pots of flour. The quern's by the fields, south of the fort.

steps.log: Bake three loaves of bread from flour on a range or a campfire, and bring them to Sabina.
remind: Flour on the fire, not in it. Three loaves, and don't eat them on the way.

complete: Not bad. A bit flat. The men won't notice.
Here: something for your trouble, and some seed for next year. Every soldier should know where his bread comes from.

the_smiths_apprentice.name: The Smith's Apprentice
the_smiths_apprentice.summary: The fort's smith needs a pair of hands. Mine copper and tin, smelt bronze, and forge your first blade.
start: You've got a pickaxe and a hammer and no idea what to do with either. I can fix that.
Copper and tin from the quarry, east of the fort by the road. Five of each.
Then we'll see if you can work a furnace without losing your eyebrows. I didn't.

steps.log: Mine five copper ore and five tin ore at the quarry east of the fort, and bring them to Tertius at the smithy.
remind: Five copper, five tin. The quarry's just east of the fort, by the road.

steps.log: Smelt two bronze bars at the furnace (a copper ore and a tin ore each) and show them to Tertius.
remind: The furnace, by the anvil. One copper and one tin make a bar of bronze.

steps.log: Forge a bronze pugio at the anvil (a bar, with your hammer) and bring it to Tertius.
remind: A pugio. Hammer, anvil, one bar of bronze. Every legionary's first blade, and every smith's.

complete: Not bad. It'll hold an edge, and that's all a blade has to do.
Here: a gladius I finished this morning, and a scutum I had lying about. You'll make your own at Smithing 5. A smith's apprentice shouldn't go out naked.

gifts_for_the_gods.name: Gifts for the Gods
gifts_for_the_gods.summary: The sacerdos wants offerings for the Capitoline altar: bones from the beasts you've slain, and a goat's hide.
start: The gods watch every fight, child. It's only polite to thank them for the ones you win.
Bring me five bones from what you've killed, and the hide of one of the wild goats north-east of the fort. I'll show you what to do with them.
And after that, you can offer them yourself, at any altar. The gods aren't fussy, only greedy.

steps.log: Bring the sacerdos five bones (rats and goats drop them) and a goat hide from the pasture north-east of the fort.
remind: Five bones and a goat hide. The goats graze north-east of the fort, and they won't fight back much.

complete: There. Smell that? That's Jupiter being pleased.
Take this incense. Offer it at the altar here, or bones at any altar, and you'll grow in the gods' favour. Blessings come with it.

the_mountain_copper.name: The Mountain-Copper
the_mountain_copper.summary: Red-gold veins have been found at the bottom of the Vipasca pit. The procurator wants to know if it's really orichalcum.
start: My diggers swear there's orichalcum in the pit floor. Orichalcum! Plato's metal, the roofs of Atlantis.
I've heard it before, and it was copper and wishful thinking. Masculus will know. Take him some of the ore, and if he's satisfied, smelt it.
If it's real, the governor will make me a rich man. I'll make you a slightly less rich one.

steps.log: Mine three orichalcum ores from the red-gold veins at the bottom of the Vipasca pit, and show them to Foreman Masculus.
remind: Three lumps of the red stuff, from the bottom of the pit. Then we'll talk.

steps.log: Smelt an orichalcum bar (an ore and four coal, Smithing 50) and bring it to the procurator.
remind: A bar. One proper bar, and the governor's courier leaves tonight.

complete: Look at it glow. The governor will weep.
Here: a pickaxe headed with it, the first ever made at Vipasca. Don't lose it in a hole.

centurion.name: Centurion
centurion.summary: Varro has put your name forward for a century. The legate in Rome will want to see what you're made of before he gives you the vine stick.
start: A letter came from Rome. The legate needs centurions, and I gave him your name.
Don't make me regret it. Take the ship from Portus Salis and report to Legate Sertorius in the forum.

steps.log: Report to Legate Sertorius in Rome's forum.
remind: The legate is in Rome. The forum, by the basilica.
say: Varro's optio. He says you don't lose men. Let's see.
The raiders beyond the Limes have been killing my road crews. Clear them off the road: ten of them.

steps.log: Kill ten Germanic raiders beyond the Limes for the legate.
remind: Ten raiders. They're beyond the Limes, where they always are.

steps.log: Report back to Legate Sertorius.
remind: Back to the legate in Rome.
say: Good. Now something no road crew could do.
There's a basilisk king under the mines at Vipasca. The procurator wants his miners back. Kill it, and bring me a fang to show the Senate.

steps.log: Kill Regulus, the basilisk king, in Vipasca's deep gallery, and take a fang as proof.
remind: Regulus. A mirror shield, or his crown if you have one.

steps.log: Bring the legate the fang, and ten steel pila for your new century.
remind: The fang, and pila for your men. A centurion doesn't arrive empty-handed.

complete: A fang as long as my hand. The Senate will like that.
Kneel. No, I'm joking. Take this: the vitis. It means you may strike a citizen, and every man in your century will know it.
And the crest, so they can find you in a fight. Centurion.

rewards.title: Centurio legionis
rewards.unlocks: The vitis and the centurion's galea
